rationale: FIGO leiomyoma subclassification (Munro 2011) is a high-yield anchor for fibroid classification
Red (carneous) degeneration is the classic high-yield degeneration of pregnancy — students must distinguish it from others
POP-Q staging point C location is the defining anchor for uterine descent — students often confuse it with clinical grades
Manchester (Fothergill) repair vs vaginal hysterectomy is a common MCQ trap — students must know the correct indication
Route of HRT delivery is an important clinical decision — transdermal avoids first-pass hepatic effect and has lower VTE risk than oral
The definition of menopause (12 months amenorrhoea) is foundational and must be memorised precisely
The TVS endometrial thickness cut-off (4 mm in postmenopausal, not on HRT) is a key investigative rule that students must apply correctly
Endometrial carcinoma type I vs II distinction is fundamental — oestrogen-dependent vs p53-driven pathway
The revised ASRM (rASRM) staging of endometriosis — students must know it is based on laparoscopic findings, not symptoms
Medical management of endometriosis — GnRH agonist add-back therapy is a high-yield clinical scenario
